channel.name: Arirang World KR
channel.title: K-CHAT: CONVERSING IN KOREAN

A comprehensive Korean program designed to teach Korean language through real-life situations! A global initiative featuring top performers. Engage in lively Korean language lessons taught by Korean-American idols Aaron and Alexa! Experience a delightful Korean language course that delves into culture, trends, and even generational nuances. Each lesson is a concise 10-minute package, including scenarios, explanations, and practical exercises. Enjoy short, yet entertaining content that will also provide insight into culture, trends, and generational diversity. With just a glance, you'll be able to speak Korean fluently. It also covers traditional Korean culture and essential travel information, making it an invaluable resource for beginner to intermediate learners! Discover Korean travel expressions in an engaging and entertaining way with skits performed by ONF?s Hyo-jin, Seung-jun, Wyatt, and Alexa. With clear and accessible explanations from Hye-rim of the Wonder Girls, a graduate of Hankuk University of Foreign Studies, you?ll systematically improve your Korean!

channel.name: Arirang World KR
channel.title: EXPLORING KOREAN LITERATURE B
channel.desc:
2021 Exploring Korean Literature There is a growing interest in Korean literature among readers from around the world and so we bring Korean classics to Korean modern literature to viewers in this special series under three themes. What They?ve Read Well-known TV personalities read three translated works of Korean literature that have recently received attention. Kim Soom's novel \"One Left\", brings the comfort women issue to the forefront of the literary world, and her book is recited and discussed by Darcy Paquet, a translator and essayist for the film \"Parasite,\" and translator and essayist Colin Marshall, Italian architect Simone Carena, and fashion designer Shin Ji-hye. The novel was published in the U.S. in September 2020 and a second book print was released this year. Cho Nam-Joo's novel \"Kim Jiyoung, Born 1982\" has been translated into 25 languages and is recited by TV personality Daniel Hicks (UK), Carlos Gorito (Brazil), YouTuber Sarah Mack (USA) and singer Punita (India) who share their thoughts about the book. Howon, a member of the boy band, W24, recites passages from Kim Young-ha's novel \"Diary of a Murderer\" and gives commentary. Living to Tell a Story This documentary features Korean writers whose works are not only popular in Korea but also overseas. In episode 1, poet Kim Yi-deum, the Winner of the National Translation Award and the Lucien Stryk Award for her collection of poems, \"Hysteria,\" as well as Korean novelists Kim Cho-Yup and Kim Yeon-su appear to talk about the creative process and how they carry out research before writing a novel. In Episode 2, novelist Yun Ko-Eun, the winner of the Crime Fiction in Translation Dagger award for her book, \"The Disaster Tourist\", and novelist Ha Seong-nan and poet Jin Eun-young explain what they were trying to convey to readers through their works. In Episode 3, novelist Hwang Sok-young, whose works are mostly inspired by his own experience of living in modern Korean society, tells the story of his life and literary journey. A Word Depicted in Stories The cultural characteristics in Korean literature that encompasses Korean classics to modern novels are highlighted on this show. Six episodes with different themes ranging from female poets in classical literature, makeup culture, wine and arts, tea ceremony, pets, and a literary discussion forum will begin airing on November 5th. -->
.

channel.name: Arirang World KR
channel.title: EXPLORING KOREAN LITERATURE B
channel.desc:
2021 Exploring Korean Literature There is a growing interest in Korean literature among readers from around the world and so we bring Korean classics to Korean modern literature to viewers in this special series under three themes. What They?ve Read Well-known TV personalities read three translated works of Korean literature that have recently received attention. Kim Soom's novel \"One Left\", brings the comfort women issue to the forefront of the literary world, and her book is recited and discussed by Darcy Paquet, a translator and essayist for the film \"Parasite,\" and translator and essayist Colin Marshall, Italian architect Simone Carena, and fashion designer Shin Ji-hye. The novel was published in the U.S. in September 2020 and a second book print was released this year. Cho Nam-Joo's novel \"Kim Jiyoung, Born 1982\" has been translated into 25 languages and is recited by TV personality Daniel Hicks (UK), Carlos Gorito (Brazil), YouTuber Sarah Mack (USA) and singer Punita (India) who share their thoughts about the book. Howon, a member of the boy band, W24, recites passages from Kim Young-ha's novel \"Diary of a Murderer\" and gives commentary. Living to Tell a Story This documentary features Korean writers whose works are not only popular in Korea but also overseas. In episode 1, poet Kim Yi-deum, the Winner of the National Translation Award and the Lucien Stryk Award for her collection of poems, \"Hysteria,\" as well as Korean novelists Kim Cho-Yup and Kim Yeon-su appear to talk about the creative process and how they carry out research before writing a novel. In Episode 2, novelist Yun Ko-Eun, the winner of the Crime Fiction in Translation Dagger award for her book, \"The Disaster Tourist\", and novelist Ha Seong-nan and poet Jin Eun-young explain what they were trying to convey to readers through their works. In Episode 3, novelist Hwang Sok-young, whose works are mostly inspired by his own experience of living in modern Korean society, tells the story of his life and literary journey. A Word Depicted in Stories The cultural characteristics in Korean literature that encompasses Korean classics to modern novels are highlighted on this show. Six episodes with different themes ranging from female poets in classical literature, makeup culture, wine and arts, tea ceremony, pets, and a literary discussion forum will begin airing on November 5th. -->

channel.name: Arirang World KR
channel.title: EXPLORING KOREAN LITERATURE C
channel.desc:
2021 Exploring Korean Literature There is a growing interest in Korean literature among readers from around the world and so we bring Korean classics to Korean modern literature to viewers in this special series under three themes. What They?ve Read Well-known TV personalities read three translated works of Korean literature that have recently received attention. Kim Soom's novel \"One Left\", brings the comfort women issue to the forefront of the literary world, and her book is recited and discussed by Darcy Paquet, a translator and essayist for the film \"Parasite,\" and translator and essayist Colin Marshall, Italian architect Simone Carena, and fashion designer Shin Ji-hye. The novel was published in the U.S. in September 2020 and a second book print was released this year. Cho Nam-Joo's novel \"Kim Jiyoung, Born 1982\" has been translated into 25 languages and is recited by TV personality Daniel Hicks (UK), Carlos Gorito (Brazil), YouTuber Sarah Mack (USA) and singer Punita (India) who share their thoughts about the book. Howon, a member of the boy band, W24, recites passages from Kim Young-ha's novel \"Diary of a Murderer\" and gives commentary. Living to Tell a Story This documentary features Korean writers whose works are not only popular in Korea but also overseas. In episode 1, poet Kim Yi-deum, the Winner of the National Translation Award and the Lucien Stryk Award for her collection of poems, \"Hysteria,\" as well as Korean novelists Kim Cho-Yup and Kim Yeon-su appear to talk about the creative process and how they carry out research before writing a novel. In Episode 2, novelist Yun Ko-Eun, the winner of the Crime Fiction in Translation Dagger award for her book, \"The Disaster Tourist\", and novelist Ha Seong-nan and poet Jin Eun-young explain what they were trying to convey to readers through their works. In Episode 3, novelist Hwang Sok-young, whose works are mostly inspired by his own experience of living in modern Korean society, tells the story of his life and literary journey. A Word Depicted in Stories The cultural characteristics in Korean literature that encompasses Korean classics to modern novels are highlighted on this show. Six episodes with different themes ranging from female poets in classical literature, makeup culture, wine and arts, tea ceremony, pets, and a literary discussion forum will begin airing on November 5th. -->

channel.title: EXPLORING KOREAN LITERATURE A
channel.desc:
2021 Exploring Korean Literature There is a growing interest in Korean literature among readers from around the world and so we bring Korean classics to Korean modern literature to viewers in this special series under three themes. What They?ve Read Well-known TV personalities read three translated works of Korean literature that have recently received attention. Kim Soom's novel \"One Left\", brings the comfort women issue to the forefront of the literary world, and her book is recited and discussed by Darcy Paquet, a translator and essayist for the film \"Parasite,\" and translator and essayist Colin Marshall, Italian architect Simone Carena, and fashion designer Shin Ji-hye. The novel was published in the U.S. in September 2020 and a second book print was released this year. Cho Nam-Joo's novel \"Kim Jiyoung, Born 1982\" has been translated into 25 languages and is recited by TV personality Daniel Hicks (UK), Carlos Gorito (Brazil), YouTuber Sarah Mack (USA) and singer Punita (India) who share their thoughts about the book. Howon, a member of the boy band, W24, recites passages from Kim Young-ha's novel \"Diary of a Murderer\" and gives commentary. Living to Tell a Story This documentary features Korean writers whose works are not only popular in Korea but also overseas. In episode 1, poet Kim Yi-deum, the Winner of the National Translation Award and the Lucien Stryk Award for her collection of poems, \"Hysteria,\" as well as Korean novelists Kim Cho-Yup and Kim Yeon-su appear to talk about the creative process and how they carry out research before writing a novel. In Episode 2, novelist Yun Ko-Eun, the winner of the Crime Fiction in Translation Dagger award for her book, \"The Disaster Tourist\", and novelist Ha Seong-nan and poet Jin Eun-young explain what they were trying to convey to readers through their works. In Episode 3, novelist Hwang Sok-young, whose works are mostly inspired by his own experience of living in modern Korean society, tells the story of his life and literary journey. A Word Depicted in Stories The cultural characteristics in Korean literature that encompasses Korean classics to modern novels are highlighted on this show. Six episodes with different themes ranging from female poets in classical literature, makeup culture, wine and arts, tea ceremony, pets, and a literary discussion forum will begin airing on November 5th. -->

channel.name: Arirang World KR
channel.title: EXPLORING KOREAN LITERATURE A
channel.desc:
2021 Exploring Korean Literature There is a growing interest in Korean literature among readers from around the world and so we bring Korean classics to Korean modern literature to viewers in this special series under three themes. What They?ve Read Well-known TV personalities read three translated works of Korean literature that have recently received attention. Kim Soom's novel \"One Left\", brings the comfort women issue to the forefront of the literary world, and her book is recited and discussed by Darcy Paquet, a translator and essayist for the film \"Parasite,\" and translator and essayist Colin Marshall, Italian architect Simone Carena, and fashion designer Shin Ji-hye. The novel was published in the U.S. in September 2020 and a second book print was released this year. Cho Nam-Joo's novel \"Kim Jiyoung, Born 1982\" has been translated into 25 languages and is recited by TV personality Daniel Hicks (UK), Carlos Gorito (Brazil), YouTuber Sarah Mack (USA) and singer Punita (India) who share their thoughts about the book. Howon, a member of the boy band, W24, recites passages from Kim Young-ha's novel \"Diary of a Murderer\" and gives commentary. Living to Tell a Story This documentary features Korean writers whose works are not only popular in Korea but also overseas. In episode 1, poet Kim Yi-deum, the Winner of the National Translation Award and the Lucien Stryk Award for her collection of poems, \"Hysteria,\" as well as Korean novelists Kim Cho-Yup and Kim Yeon-su appear to talk about the creative process and how they carry out research before writing a novel. In Episode 2, novelist Yun Ko-Eun, the winner of the Crime Fiction in Translation Dagger award for her book, \"The Disaster Tourist\", and novelist Ha Seong-nan and poet Jin Eun-young explain what they were trying to convey to readers through their works. In Episode 3, novelist Hwang Sok-young, whose works are mostly inspired by his own experience of living in modern Korean society, tells the story of his life and literary journey. A Word Depicted in Stories The cultural characteristics in Korean literature that encompasses Korean classics to modern novels are highlighted on this show. Six episodes with different themes ranging from female poets in classical literature, makeup culture, wine and arts, tea ceremony, pets, and a literary discussion forum will begin airing on November 5th. -->
.

channel.name: Arirang World KR
channel.title: DIVE INTO KOREAN
channel.desc: ?Dive into Korean? is an introductory educational documentary series designed for learners beginning their journey with the Korean language. The program explores the historical and cultural essence of Hangeul, the Korean alphabet, and the spirit behind its creation by King Sejong the Great. Through engaging storytelling and real-life experiences, the series helps viewers understand the beauty, science, and philosophy embedded in the Korean language. Episode 1: Hangeul ? A Script Anyone Can Learn Easily Discover how Hangeul was designed as an easy and logical writing system for all people, embodying King Sejong?s vision of communication and equality. Episode 2: Hangeul ? A Script That Illustrates the Sounds of Speech Explore the scientific principles behind Hangeul?s creation ? how its characters visually represent the shape and movement of the human speech organs. Episode 3: The More You Know the Culture, the Closer You Get to Korean Understand how culture and language intertwine, and how learning about Korean traditions and expressions brings learners closer to authentic communication. Episode 4: Korean Language Connecting the World Witness how Korean has grown into a global language of culture, creativity, and connection ? a bridge linking people across nations.\"Sponsored by King Sejong Institute Foundation\".

channel.name: Arirang World KR
channel.title: EXPLORING KOREAN LITERATURE A
channel.desc:
2021 Exploring Korean Literature There is a growing interest in Korean literature among readers from around the world and so we bring Korean classics to Korean modern literature to viewers in this special series under three themes. What They?ve Read Well-known TV personalities read three translated works of Korean literature that have recently received attention. Kim Soom's novel \"One Left\", brings the comfort women issue to the forefront of the literary world, and her book is recited and discussed by Darcy Paquet, a translator and essayist for the film \"Parasite,\" and translator and essayist Colin Marshall, Italian architect Simone Carena, and fashion designer Shin Ji-hye. The novel was published in the U.S. in September 2020 and a second book print was released this year. Cho Nam-Joo's novel \"Kim Jiyoung, Born 1982\" has been translated into 25 languages and is recited by TV personality Daniel Hicks (UK), Carlos Gorito (Brazil), YouTuber Sarah Mack (USA) and singer Punita (India) who share their thoughts about the book. Howon, a member of the boy band, W24, recites passages from Kim Young-ha's novel \"Diary of a Murderer\" and gives commentary. Living to Tell a Story This documentary features Korean writers whose works are not only popular in Korea but also overseas. In episode 1, poet Kim Yi-deum, the Winner of the National Translation Award and the Lucien Stryk Award for her collection of poems, \"Hysteria,\" as well as Korean novelists Kim Cho-Yup and Kim Yeon-su appear to talk about the creative process and how they carry out research before writing a novel. In Episode 2, novelist Yun Ko-Eun, the winner of the Crime Fiction in Translation Dagger award for her book, \"The Disaster Tourist\", and novelist Ha Seong-nan and poet Jin Eun-young explain what they were trying to convey to readers through their works. In Episode 3, novelist Hwang Sok-young, whose works are mostly inspired by his own experience of living in modern Korean society, tells the story of his life and literary journey. A Word Depicted in Stories The cultural characteristics in Korean literature that encompasses Korean classics to modern novels are highlighted on this show. Six episodes with different themes ranging from female poets in classical literature, makeup culture, wine and arts, tea ceremony, pets, and a literary discussion forum will begin airing on November 5th. -->
.

channel.name: Arirang World KR
channel.title: DIVE INTO KOREAN
channel.desc: ?Dive into Korean? is an introductory educational documentary series designed for learners beginning their journey with the Korean language. The program explores the historical and cultural essence of Hangeul, the Korean alphabet, and the spirit behind its creation by King Sejong the Great. Through engaging storytelling and real-life experiences, the series helps viewers understand the beauty, science, and philosophy embedded in the Korean language. Episode 1: Hangeul ? A Script Anyone Can Learn Easily Discover how Hangeul was designed as an easy and logical writing system for all people, embodying King Sejong?s vision of communication and equality. Episode 2: Hangeul ? A Script That Illustrates the Sounds of Speech Explore the scientific principles behind Hangeul?s creation ? how its characters visually represent the shape and movement of the human speech organs. Episode 3: The More You Know the Culture, the Closer You Get to Korean Understand how culture and language intertwine, and how learning about Korean traditions and expressions brings learners closer to authentic communication. Episode 4: Korean Language Connecting the World Witness how Korean has grown into a global language of culture, creativity, and connection ? a bridge linking people across nations.\"Sponsored by King Sejong Institute Foundation\".

channel.name: Classica IT
channel.title: Krystian Zimerman
channel.desc: Il pianista polacco Krystian Zimerman, nella duplice veste di solista e direttore, interpreta il secondo concerto che Beethoven dedico' al pianoforte - K.Zimerman, dir. e pf. - Wiener Philharmoniker \(1992\).

channel.name: Classica IT
channel.title: Stravinskij - La sagra della primavera
channel.desc: Concerto della partitura scritta da Stravinskij per il balletto messo in scena, con grande scandalo, a Parigi nel 1913 - Verbier Festival Orchestra - Daniel Harding, dir. \(Verbier, 2010\).

channel.name: Classica IT
channel.title: Il lago dei cigni - V.Kovtun, cor
channel.desc: Balletto in quattro atti \(1876\) su musica di Cajkovskij - con Natalia Matsak, Denys Nedak, Yaroslav Tkachuk - Kiev National Ballet - Kiev Opera Orch. - Valery Kovtun, cor., da M.Petipa, L.Ivanov, A.Gorski \(Kiev, 2019\).

channel.name: Classica IT
channel.title: Almanacco di Bellezza
channel.desc: Piero Maranghi, direttore di Classica HD, passa in rassegna, anniversari e ricorrenze legati la mondo dell'arte, della cultura, della storia e dello sport. In studio con lui, il collezionista ed esperto d'arte Leonardo Piccinini.

channel.name: Classica IT
channel.title: Prokof'ev - Matrimonio al convento
channel.desc: Opera lirico-comica \(1940\) in quattro atti su libretto di Prokof'ev e Mira Mendelson - con L.Diadkova, N.Gassiev - Orchestra del Teatro Mariinskij-Opera Kirov - V.Gergiev, dir. - V.Pazi, reg. \(San Pietroburgo, 1997\).

channel.name: Classica IT
channel.title: La classica domanda - Natalia Aspesi
channel.desc: Proseguono le interviste condotte da Anton Giulio Onofri a personalita' del mondo della cultura e dello spettacolo. Ospite di questa puntata della Classica domanda e' la giornalista e scrittrice Natalia Aspesi \(2014\).

channel.name: Classica IT
channel.title: Ensemble Pygmalion - Haendel e Bach
channel.desc: Il direttore francese Raphael Pichon e il suo Ensemble Pygmalion in un concerto su musiche di Georg Friedrich Haendel e Johann Sebastian Bach - Sabine Devielhe, soprano - R.Pichon, dir. \(Parigi, 2021\).

channel.name: Classica IT
channel.title: Alla scoperta del Ciro di Scarlatti
channel.desc: Un'opera dimenticata ritorna alla luce al Maggio Musicale Fiorentino grazie all'Academia Montis Regalis. Il Ciro di A.Scarlatti in prima esecuzione in epoca moderna, dopo la prima del 1712 con le scene di F.Juvarra.

channel.name: Classica IT
channel.title: Liszt - Apres une Lecture de Dante
channel.desc: Il pianista russo Arcadi Volodos esegue in concerto una selezione di brani di A.N.Skryabin e la Fantasia quasi sonata, o Dante Sonata, di F.Liszt \(1849\) ispirata alla Divina Commedia - \(Musikverein, Vienna - 2009\).

channel.name: Classica IT
channel.title: Incontri contemporanei - Del Corno
channel.desc: Protagonista della puntata e' il compositore milanese Filippo Del Corno \(classe 1970\), autore dell'opera Non guardate al domani sull'assassinio di Aldo Moro e autore affermato anche all'estero - a cura di A.Daveri \(2009\).

channel.name: Classica IT
channel.title: Krystian Zimerman
channel.desc: Il pianista polacco Krystian Zimerman, nella duplice veste di solista e direttore, interpreta il secondo concerto che Beethoven dedico' al pianoforte - K.Zimerman, dir. e pf. - Wiener Philharmoniker \(1992\).

channel.name: Classica IT
channel.title: Mozart - Sonata per violino KV 378
channel.desc: Sonata in si bemolle maggiore per violino e pianoforte in tre movimenti composta da Mozart a Salisburgo nel 1779 - Anne-Sophie Mutter, violino - Lambert Orkis, pianoforte \(Monaco di Baviera, Philharmonie - 2006\).

channel.name: Classica IT
channel.title: Verdi - Rigoletto
channel.desc: Opera in tre atti \(1851\) su libretto di F.M.Piave - con L.Avetisyan, C.Alvarez, L.Oropesa, B.Sherratt - Orchestra of the Royal Opera House - Antonio Pappano, dir. - Oliver Mears, reg. \(Londra, Covent Garden - 2021\).

channel.name: Classica IT
channel.title: Minkus - La Bayadere
channel.desc: Balletto in quattro atti \(1877\) su musica di L.Minkus e libretto di S.Chudekov - con A.Vorontsova, V.Lebedev, S.Strelkov - Corpo di ballo Teatro Mikhailovsky - N.Duato, cor. da Marius Petipa \(S.Pietroburgo, 2020\).

channel.name: Classica IT
channel.title: Almanacco di Bellezza
channel.desc: Piero Maranghi, direttore di Classica HD, passa in rassegna, anniversari e ricorrenze legati la mondo dell'arte, della cultura, della storia e dello sport. In studio con lui, il collezionista ed esperto d'arte Leonardo Piccinini.

channel.name: Classica IT
channel.title: Herbert von Karajan
channel.desc: Alla guida dei Berliner Philharmoniker, il grande maestro austriaco dirige la Suite n.2 in si minore \(1723\) di Bach e il Concerto brandeburghese n.3 in sol maggiore BWV 1048 \(1713\) in un'esecuzione del 1967.

channel.name: Classica IT
channel.title: Ensemble Pygmalion - Haendel e Bach
channel.desc: Il direttore francese Raphael Pichon e il suo Ensemble Pygmalion in un concerto su musiche di Georg Friedrich Haendel e Johann Sebastian Bach - Sabine Devielhe, soprano - R.Pichon, dir. \(Parigi, 2021\).

channel.name: Classica IT
channel.title: La Classica domanda - Peppe Vessicchio
channel.desc: Anton Giulio Onofri intervista le personalita' del mondo dello spettacolo e della cultura italiana. Ospite della Classica Domanda di oggi e' il compositore e direttore d'orchestra Peppe Vessicchio, da poco scomparso \(2017\).

channel.name: Classica IT
channel.title: Discovering Beethoven - ep.2
channel.desc: Christian Thielemann ci accompagna alla scoperta della Sinfonia n.2 in re maggiore op.36, composta da Beethoven nel 1802 e suddivisa in 4 movimenti - con il musicologo Joachim Kaiser \(2011\).

channel.name: Classica IT
channel.title: Beethoven - Sinfonia n.2
channel.desc: Sinfonia in re maggiore op.36, composta da Beethoven nel 1802 durante un soggiorno a Heiligenstadt ed eseguita a Vienna nel 1805 sotto la direzione dell'autore - Wiener Philharmoniker - Christian Thielemann, direttore.

channel.name: Classica IT
channel.title: Andrea Bacchetti - Recital pt.2
channel.desc: Il pianista Andrea Bacchetti ritorna al Festival Pianistico Internazionale di Brescia e Bergamo con un vasto repertorio - Musiche di Cimarosa, Scarlatti, Mozart, Schubert - A.Bacchetti, pf. \(Brescia, San Barnaba - 2023\).

channel.name: Classica IT
channel.title: Beethoven - Sinfonia n.6
channel.desc: Sinfonia in fa maggiore - nel programma del concerto l'opera era definita come ''Sinfonia Pastorale, piuttosto espressione del sentimento che pittura'' - Berliner Philharmoniker - S.Rattle, dir. \(Praga, Castello - 2013\).

channel.desc: Hearty favorites such as blue crab, pit beef and chocolaty Berger cookies are featured as Andrew travels the gritty city.

channel.name: Cooking Channel US
channel.title: Bizarre Foods: Delicious Destinations
channel.desc: Andrew is in Seville, Spain, enjoying long nights of communal drinking and eating cured Iberico ham, gazpacho and serranito pork sandwiches.

channel.name: Cooking Channel US
channel.title: Bizarre Foods: Delicious Destinations
channel.desc: Andrew spotlights Goa, a former Portuguese colony and lush tropical paradise on the western coast of India, where the seaside city's local cuisine, including prawn curry, Portuguese chorizo and pork vindaloo, is influenced by many different cultures.

channel.name: Cooking Channel US
channel.title: Bizarre Foods: Delicious Destinations
channel.desc: Andrew Zimmern samples the culinary mashups of Trinidad and Tobago, including curried crab with dumplings, crispy fried shark sandwiches and soft flatbreads perfect for scooping veggies and curries.

channel.name: Cooking Channel US
channel.title: Burgers, Brew & 'Que
channel.desc: A chocolate bacon burger is loaded from top to bottom; a soy-marinated pineapple hanger steak draped over spicy kimchi fried rice; fried potato cakes loaded with brisket burnt ends, mustard hollandaise sauce and a perfectly runny egg.

channel.name: Cooking Channel US
channel.title: Burgers, Brew & 'Que
channel.desc: Michael Symon munches on fish tacos with house-made blue corn tortillas and a meaty Mexican pizza; a Colorado lamb patty is a remake of a traditional Hawaiian hangover cure; pulled pork and brisket sandwich; barbecue rib-meat chimichanga.

channel.name: Cooking Channel US
channel.title: Burgers, Brew & 'Que
channel.desc: Michael Symon devours towering burgers piled with spicy Korean pork bulgogi and juicy pork belly pastrami; a modern-day sloppy joe is loaded with burnt brisket ends; lamb-chili tacos and cheesy shawarma nachos.

channel.name: Cooking Channel US
channel.title: Burgers, Brew & 'Que
channel.desc: Michael Symon devours a meaty stacked sandwich and a beefy ballpark dog; a gas station-turned-burger joint serves a fried apple and brie cheeseburger; homemade deep-fried sausage and Cajun crawfish enchiladas.

channel.name: Cooking Channel US
channel.title: Carnival Eats
channel.desc: Noah Cappe feels the brotherly love at the RiverRink Festival in Philadelphia with the ultimate crab fries; he checks out the South Florida Fair for the pizza supreme blossom and Las Vegas' Great American Foodie Fest for divine lobster 'n waffles.

channel.name: Cooking Channel US
channel.title: Carnival Eats
channel.desc: These fairground vendors have combined two iconic treats into one revolutionary new midway masterpiece.

channel.name: Cooking Channel US
channel.title: Carnival Eats
channel.desc: Noah visits the Houston Livestock Show and Rodeo and samples the Texas Chili Burger and the Big Texas Barbecue Baked Potato; Lemonade Days in Dunwoody, Ga., for the Rise & Shine Pizza; a sushi burrito; the wacky Funnel Cake Dog.

channel.name: Cooking Channel US
channel.title: Carnival Eats
channel.desc: Caliente curls; chile relleno dog; mac and cheese bacon burger; cowboy beans; the Sunnyside burger; tropical tantalizer.

channel.name: Cooking Channel US
channel.title: Food Paradise
channel.desc: Carolina Reaper hot wings, a stacked Nashville hot chicken sandwich, hot fudge and hot tamales are among the hottest dishes in town.

channel.name: Cooking Channel US
channel.title: Holiday Baking Championship
channel.desc: Jesse Palmer asks the 10 bakers to highlight a nut or seed in a holiday dessert; then, the competitors must use a fundamental holiday ingredient in unseasonable desserts, like icebox cakes or fruit tarts.

channel.name: Cooking Channel US
channel.title: Holiday Baking Championship
channel.desc: Host Jesse Palmer asks the nine bakers to make holiday cookie-topped mini pies; the competitors celebrate fall with flavor combos; pumpkin-cider and chestnut-chocolate in cream pies; lattice pies.

channel.name: Cooking Channel US
channel.title: Holiday Baking Championship
channel.desc: The challenge for the eight bakers is to turn breakfast items into Thanksgiving desserts; Friendsgiving potluck-inspired desserts are made to impress judges Nancy Fuller, Duff Goldman and Carla Hall.[(96057)]

channel.desc: Mother Angelica provides insights from Matthew about forgiveness. By choosing to forgive, the soul is beautifully transformed into Jesus, and instead of remaining self-centered, we become others-centered, like Christ. (30 minutes).

channel.name: EWTN ZA
channel.title: The Church Universal
channel.desc: Members of the Catholic Medical Association join Fr. Joseph to explain how they help doctors, nurses, and medical students stay strong in their faith. (30 minutes).

channel.name: EWTN ZA
channel.title: Kibeho: Listen, My Children
channel.desc: In this origInal docudrama, you?ll learn the story behind the miraculous visions of the Blessed Virgin Mary in Kibeho, Rwanda in the 1980?s. Her dire warnings and prophetic visions foreshadowed the genocide to come. (60 minutes).

channel.name: EWTN ZA
channel.title: Living The Works Of Mercy
channel.desc: Father Andrew Apostoli, C.F.R., looks at some of the apostolic activities of the Franciscan Friars and Sisters of the Renewal, and explains how caring for the homeless can be an act of love for Christ who was homeless during his public ministry. (30 minutes).

channel.name: EWTN ZA
channel.title: Chaplet Of Divine Mercy
channel.desc: From the chapel of the National Shrine of the Divine Mercy in Stockbridge, Massachusetts. (20 minutes).

channel.name: EWTN ZA
channel.title: Reflections With Fr. Leo Clifford
channel.desc: Father Leo Clifford develops this talk around our names and what we do to identify ourselves to others. He shows various ways St. John the Evangelist is known and goes on to say that we are the masters of our own fate in how we are known to the world. (10 minutes).

channel.name: EWTN ZA
channel.title: Church And The Poor
channel.desc: Father Ho Lung continues his examination of the relationship between the liturgy and daily life, explaining that just as the bread and wine are transformed into Christ?s Body and Blood at the Consecration , so loving service to those in need transforms the mystical body. (30 minutes).

channel.name: EWTN ZA
channel.title: The Path To Holiness
channel.desc: Grace MacKinnon continues her lecture series on Dietrich Von Hildebrand?s monumental book, "Transformation in Christ.," with this segment focusing on the Church?s teaching regarding contrition and the Sacrament of Reconciliation. (30 minutes).

channel.name: EWTN ZA
channel.title: Holy Bears: It's Great To Be Alive
channel.desc: Two teddy bears are shipwrecked on a remote island but after restoring a young girl's faith, they embark on a special mission to aid other suffering children. (30 minutes).[(96057)]

channel.desc: Approximately 51 percent of the U.S. population is made up of women, but on "Outnumbered" the female advantage jumps to a 4-1 ratio. The hourlong show features a rotating panel of four women and one man discussing the day's headlines from various perspectives. In addition to the top news of the hour, the panelists discuss leading pop culture and relationship issues making headlines that day. Regular FNC and FBN contributors appearing on the show on a rotational basis include Harris Faulkner, Meghan McCain and Pete Hegseth.

channel.name: Fox News US
channel.title: Live: The Story With Martha MacCallum
channel.desc: Martha MacCallum has been part of the Fox News family for a number of years but made the jump to prime time while chronicling the first 100 days of President Trump's administration. Now she's branching out to cover all of the happenings in the nation's capital on "The Story." She keeps viewers up-to-date on the critical decisions, political maneuvers and key developments coming out of D.C. Through interviews with guests and reports from the network's roster of correspondents, MacCallum goes in-depth on the stories that matter to viewers.

The hosts also conclude each show by selecting a topic of their choice for the "One More Thing" segment.

channel.name: Fox News US
channel.title: Live: The Ingraham Angle
channel.desc: Laura Ingraham is one of the most listened to women on political talk radio in the country. Ingraham earned a B.A. degree at Dartmouth college and a Juris Doctor degree at the University of Virginia School of Law. She took the knowledge from her J.D. degree and applied it to serve as a litigator and Supreme Court law clerk. She is also the best-selling author of five books. Tune in to watch"The Ingraham Angle," as the program serves to discuss the issues that are being overlooked and other issues that are causing turmoil in the United States.

channel.title: Live: The Ingraham Angle
channel.desc: Laura Ingraham is one of the most listened to women on political talk radio in the country. Ingraham earned a B.A. degree at Dartmouth college and a Juris Doctor degree at the University of Virginia School of Law. She took the knowledge from her J.D. degree and applied it to serve as a litigator and Supreme Court law clerk. She is also the best-selling author of five books. Tune in to watch"The Ingraham Angle," as the program serves to discuss the issues that are being overlooked and other issues that are causing turmoil in the United States.

Not big enough for large panels, multiple boards must be glued together, leading to uneven coloring. The answer, to dye the furniture with indigo, transforming each piece into a unified whole. This clever idea and their love of wood itself gives their work an inner beauty that's attracting real interest.

channel.name: NHK World JP
channel.title: Darwin's Amazing Animals
channel.desc: Japanese pond turtles live in the rivers and ponds of Japan. Recently, however, the species has been designated as near threatened due to environmental changes and the presence of invasive species. However, during a six-month tracking project, researchers found that they actually take full advantage of the rich Satoyama landscape areas. They feed on insects in rice paddies, fruits in the woods and tomatoes in the fields. The team also discovered that they even lay eggs in agricultural greenhouses. This episode looks through the eyes of these amazing creatures to reveal their surprising way of life.

channel.name: NHK World JP
channel.title: Time Lapse Journey
channel.desc: Iwate Prefecture is home to many historic sites which were made to represent Buddhist paradise. Chuson-ji Temple in Hiraizumi, a World Heritage Site, is home to the golden Konjikido hall which offers a prayer for peace. The garden in Motsu-ji Temple was made as a depiction of paradise and has been also registered as a World Heritage Site. Catch a glimpse of eternity through time-lapse photography.

channel.name: NHK World JP
channel.title: Matsuri: The Heartbeat Of Japan
channel.desc: In Kurume, Fukuoka Prefecture, the first week of the new year culminates in Oniyo: the night of the oni, or demon. Six giant torches, measuring 13 meters and weighing 1.2 tons, are moved around a shrine precinct. They create a shadow in which the oni can emerge. One torch is taken to the river, where the oni conducts a ritual that cleanses people of their troubles. This matsuri also recounts a 1,600-year-old story about a local hero defeating an outlaw?who goes on to become the oni.

channel.title: Matsuri: The Heartbeat Of Japan
channel.desc: On New Year's Eve, performers dress as terrifying monsters called namahage. They barge into people's homes, condemning laziness and frightening children. But this good-natured tradition strengthens family and community bonds. In Tayazawa, a small village in Akita Prefecture, the practice came to an end several years ago, but was recently restarted by an enthusiastic group of locals. They made costumes and succeeded in reviving a custom at risk of slipping away.

channel.name: NHK World JP
channel.title: Matsuri: The Heartbeat Of Japan
channel.desc: On New Year's Eve, performers dress as terrifying monsters called namahage. They barge into people's homes, condemning laziness and frightening children. But this good-natured tradition strengthens family and community bonds. In Tayazawa, a small village in Akita Prefecture, the practice came to an end several years ago, but was recently restarted by an enthusiastic group of locals. They made costumes and succeeded in reviving a custom at risk of slipping away.

channel.title: Bosai: Science That Can Save Your Life
channel.desc: The number of foreign visitors to Japan has been on the rise since the COVID travel restrictions have been lifted. However, many are not fully aware of natural disasters that strike Japan such as earthquakes, tsunamis, and typhoons. Now, there are efforts to ensure the safety of visitors during disasters. The newly developed \"announcer drone\" translates text into 29 languages and instructs people to evacuate while flying. At evacuation centers, local governments are well prepared to notify important information to those who do not understand Japanese, using translation systems developed for emergency situations.

channel.name: Thrill ID
channel.title: Night Watch

channel.name: Thrill ID

channel.name: Thrill ID

channel.name: Thrill ID

channel.name: Z Living US
channel.title: The Carol Burnett Show
channel.desc: Comedian and stage actress Carol Burnett, who first gained popularity during her stint on "The Gary Moore Show," hosted this one-hour variety series. Her talented supporting players included Harvey Korman, Tim Conway, Vicki Lawrence (who got the job based on her resemblance to Burnett) and Lyle Waggoner. Skits often featured guest stars, such as Mama Cass of the Mamas and the Papas or singer Steve Lawrence. One sketch, "The Family" (which featured Lawrence as the persnickety Mama and Burnett as her hotheaded daughter) was later spun-off into it's own sitcom.

channel.name: Z Living US
channel.title: The Carol Burnett Show
channel.desc: Comedian and stage actress Carol Burnett, who first gained popularity during her stint on "The Gary Moore Show," hosted this one-hour variety series. Her talented supporting players included Harvey Korman, Tim Conway, Vicki Lawrence (who got the job based on her resemblance to Burnett) and Lyle Waggoner. Skits often featured guest stars, such as Mama Cass of the Mamas and the Papas or singer Steve Lawrence. One sketch, "The Family" (which featured Lawrence as the persnickety Mama and Burnett as her hotheaded daughter) was later spun-off into it's own sitcom.

channel.title: The Adventures of Ozzie & Harriet
channel.desc: Long-running sitcom "The Adventures of Ozzie and Harriet," based on a radio show of the same name, is one of the shows from the period that epitomized the values of the 1950s and early '60s through the all-American nuclear family. The series stars real-life married couple Ozzie and Harriet Nelson as well as their sons, David and Ricky. The focus of the series is the Nelsons' home life as they deal with run-of-the-mill problems that families of the day faced. By the time the show went off the air, it had produced 435 episodes over 14 seasons.
